newsitem.title: USA: Apria sees Q2 oper income down.
newsitem.headline: Apria sees Q2 oper income down.

text.p: Apria Healthcare Group Inc said Thursday that, excluding charges of up to $1.21 per share, it expects income from continuing operations in 1997's second quarter to be between $0.35 and $0.38 per fully diluted share, compared with $0.42 per fully diluted share for the same quarter in 1996.
Apria said it will release complete, final results for the second quarter in late July.
Apria said it expects second quarter results to include charges of up to $95 million, before taxes, of which up to $75 million relate to accounts receivable.
About one-half of the anticipated accounts receivable charge relates to a more conservative reserve position taken on accounts over 180 days, the company said.
This change in estimate is considered necessary by management because the reduction in over 180 day accounts has been slower than anticipated, the company said.

The remainder of the accounts receivable charge is a combination of revenue adjustments and an increase in the bad debt provision rate for accounts receivable less than 180 days, necessitated by billing and collection difficulties that continued into early 1997, the company said.

The company also said it expects a charge of up to $20 million for potential write-offs and accruals from exiting unprofitable business lines and to increase its reserve for excess and obsolete inventory.
Apria said it began to restructure its operations to focus more on core business lines of respiratory services, home infusion therapy and home medical equipment.
Lower-margin, non-core businesses such as subcontracted home health nursing and sales of rehabilitation equipment and medical supplies will be phased out during the balance of 1997, Apria said.

"Consistent with our 1997 objective to manage the mix of revenues and improve gross margins, we believe it is essential to focus our efforts on the three core business lines that provide the highest return," a news release issued by the company said.
